model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; cash earnings after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E net operating income on the cash-earnings basis (net interest income + other operating income, ex large notable items and hedging/fair-value volatility). FY2026 ends 30 Sep 2026 and is unreported (due Nov 2026); FY0 = 1H26 actual 10,870 (NAB.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:703) + 2H26 at run-rate ~10,980 (+1.0% HoH; 1H26 was +3.1% HoH, +5.9% YoY). FY2025 actual on the same basis was 20,813 (statutory CSV revenue 20,872). Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 exactly one year from the valuation date, which the engine's end-of-year discounting requires; anchoring on FY2025 would discount every flow a full extra year.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,061.3m ordinary shares net of treasury at 31 Mar 2026 (NAB.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:7409) plus 6m dilutive equity-based compensation rights (:7243) = 3,067m, PLUS an ESTIMATED 46m shares issued on 2 Jul 2026 under the 1H26 DRP, which carried a 1.5% discount and a $1.0bn underwrite over and above expected participation to raise ~$1.8bn in total (:657, :5304); 1.8bn / ~$39 DRP price = ~46m. The exact issue count is in NAB's July 2026 Appendix 2A, not in the extracted filings: REFRESH this anchor when the FY2026 annual report (Nov 2026) prints the year-end count. The 11m weighted potential shares from convertible capital notes are EXCLUDED: they are AT1 regulatory capital that converts at market price and their cost is already borne by shareholders (distributions charged to equity), so counting them would double-charge. Count held FLAT thereafter: equity-based compensation is expensed in the flows, and the DRP is neutralised by on-market purchases in normal years.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. NAB is an APRA-regulated ADI: bonds, notes and subordinated debt ($179.1bn at 31 Mar 2026, core_metrics) and customer deposits ($765.8bn, kpis) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and liquid assets ($11.4bn) are held against that funding and are not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (cash earnings less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = cash earnings ex-LNI ~7,190 less capital retained ~2,270 (= NPAT x g/ROTE at ~4% growth, 12.4% ROTE). Cross-check: FY2025 cash earnings 7,091 less dividends paid 5,177 and buyback 616 = 1,298 retained, but CET1 still slipped 12.35% -> 11.70% -> 11.65% (Mar-26) as RWA grew 5.5% YoY to $449.8bn; the ~$1.8bn underwritten DRP in July 2026 is the catch-up, i.e. FY2025-26 distributions ran ahead of organic FCFE. reported_fcf = FCFE + equity-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 +8,511; FY2024 -35,781; FY2023 -26,699) is deposit/loan/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow; the financial-parser left free_cash_flow empty for that reason. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Equity-based compensation $149m FY2025, $143m FY2024 (NAB.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:13252, :13269 statement of changes in equity, $m). Awards are settled from shares issued or treasury shares (4.1m shares issued for equity-based compensation in 1H26, :7407); there is no separate net-share-settlement tax line. ~0.7% of net operating income, so the house/street band is narrow.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income ($56.8bn gross, $17.4bn net FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: No buyback in 1H26 (NAB.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:4632: nil vs $616m FY2025, $2,077m FY2024; $8bn cumulative since Aug 2021). The programme is paused: NAB raised ~$1.8bn of new equity through the underwritten 1H26 DRP instead. The flat count is therefore a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows, not by repurchases, and the DRP issuance is in the base count.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-03-31 (31 Mar 2026 count, plus estimated 2 Jul 2026 DRP issuance)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Equity attributable to owners $60,561m at 31 Mar 2026 (total equity incl. $688m NCI / preference shares issued by subsidiaries); goodwill and other intangibles $4,371m (down from $5,622m at Sep-25 after the $1,347m accelerated software amortisation, :4538) -> tangible book ~$56.2bn, NTA/share $18.32 (:785). Post-DRP tangible book ~$58.0bn = ~$18.6/share on 3,113m. Cash ROE 11.4% FY2025, 11.6% 1H26 ex-LNI (8.5% incl.); ROTE on ex-LNI cash earnings ~12.4%. CET1 11.65% at Mar-26 (pro forma 12.05% post-DRP) vs >11.25% target; RWA $449.8bn.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in AUD, the currency of the flows: AUD 10-year Commonwealth bond ~4.3% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.0 x Australian equity risk premium 5.4% = 9.7%. Beta 1.0 for a domestic big-four bank (MQG.AX was set at 1.15 for its markets-facing income). One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, operational (outages, payroll remediation) and regulatory risk is charged in the bear flows and in the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial ($1.9bn liabilities vs $60.6bn equity, NAB.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:17603); lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. NCI profit share is $39m FY2025 / $19m per half (0.5% of cash earnings) and is absorbed in the 30.0% cash-tax-rate driver (29.6% effective tax on cash earnings + ~0.4% NCI leakage; 1H26 ex-LNI: 5,146 pre-tax -> 3,588 = 30.3%). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (as MQG.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX 2026-09-23). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)) and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. Engine mapping: revenue = net operating income (cash-earnings basis); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax cash profit (NOI - operating expenses ex-LNI - credit impairment charge) PLUS equity-based compensation, as % of NOI (FY2025 49.4%: 20,813 - 9,848 - 833 = 10,132 + 149; 1H26 ex-LNI 48.0%; FY2026E 47.7%); sbc_pct_path = equity-based compensation 0.7%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and amortisation are inside operating expenses; software amortisation is a genuine cost for a bank, not an add-back); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the CET1 target = NPAT margin x g/ROTE; cash_tax_rate_path = 30.0% (tax + NCI); wacc = cost of equity 9.7%; net_debt = 0. FY0 reconciliation: 21,850 x (47.7% - 0.7%) x (1 - 30%) = 7,189 vs 1H26 cash earnings ex-LNI 3,588 annualised ~7,190 and FY2025 7,091. LARGE NOTABLE ITEM: the 1H26 $949m after-tax ($1,347m pre-tax) accelerated software amortisation from raising the capitalisation threshold $5m -> $20m is excluded from the flows as a one-off; its ongoing effect (more software expensed rather than capitalised) is already in the ex-LNI 1H26 opex base the margin path starts from. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (12.4 - 2.5)/(9.7 - 2.5) = 1.375x x $18.6 = ~$25.6/share, which the engine base should approximate; the market's $38.15 = 2.05x TBV requires either ROTE ~17% or a cost of equity ~7.4%. Price is the ASX regular close, not volatile. H2 FY2026 (Apr-Sep 2026) is unreported; 31 Mar 2026 is the latest balance sheet.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is cash earnings (already after equity-based compensation): FY2021 6,558; FY2022 7,104; FY2023 7,731; FY2024 7,102; FY2025 7,091 (NAB.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:10951); FY2020 3,710 was the COVID provisioning trough, so the 5-year CAGR (13.8%) measures recovery, not trend. 3-year cash-earnings CAGR is -0.1% from the FY2022 base and -2.8%/yr from the FY2023 NIM peak. Revenue = statutory net operating income (CSV): FY2016 16,648, FY2020 17,261, FY2022 18,570, FY2025 20,872.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average net operating income growth (4.0% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), anchored between the 3/5-year revenue CAGRs (3.9-4.0%) and the 9-year CAGR (2.5%); system credit growth 7.3% in FY2025 is offset by NIM competition (Personal Banking) and NAB's ~10-11% share of a mature market.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (0.5%) diverges >30% from revenue (3.9%) and EPS: book value is held flat by design (FY2021-25 dividends 5.0-5.2bn/yr plus $8bn of buybacks distributed ~100% of cash earnings), so equity CAGR does not describe the earnings power. EPS 5-year CAGR (21.9%) is measured from the FY2020 COVID trough (82c) and 3-year (1.1%) from the FY2022 base; neither is a trend. Growth is taken from the revenue and cash-earnings series.

base.growth_rationale: Net operating income. FY27 4.0%: 1H26 was +5.9% YoY on NIM 1.81% (+11bp) and business lending +9%, but RBA/RBNZ easing compresses deposit margins and Personal Banking is being repriced by brokers; volume growth ~5-6% less ~1.5pp margin drift. Tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP ~4.5% less structural margin compression), in line with the 9-year 2.5% revenue CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax cash profit + SBC on NOI. FY2026E 47.7% = 100 - CTI ex-LNI 46.8% - CIC 6.2% + SBC 0.7%. FY27 47.4%: cost growth held near income growth (>$450m productivity vs technology/compliance inflation and payroll remediation), CIC normalising from 1H26's annualised ~18bp to ~19bp (7.0% of NOI; FY18-19 ran 14-16bp, FY23-25 10-11bp). Mature 47.2% = 100 - CTI 46.5 - CIC 7.0 + 0.7. FY2025 actual was 49.4% on an 11bp CIC; the model does not assume that benign credit repeats.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at the >11.25% target as RWA grows with income = NPAT margin (32.6% of NOI) x g / ROTE 12.5% = 2.6 x g. At 4% growth 10.4% of NOI (~$2.4bn, 32% of cash earnings retained -> 68% distributed); at 2.5% terminal growth 6.5% (~20% retained -> 80% distributed, which is NAB's 65-75% dividend payout plus DRP neutralisation and modest buybacks). Cross-check on CET1: 4% RWA growth on $52bn of CET1 capital needs ~$2.1bn.

bull.growth_rationale: Business and Private Banking keeps compounding at 8-9% and holds share; proprietary mortgage mix rises past 50% so Personal Banking stops losing margin; BNZ rides the NZ recovery; NIM holds ~1.80%. NOI grows 6% FY27 fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Productivity and AI/digital cost-out take CTI to ~44% by FY30 (FY2023 was 45.4%) and credit stays benign at ~6% of NOI (~16bp): 100 - 44 - 6 + 0.7 = 50.7, held at 50.0.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin 34.5% x g / ROTE 14%: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return. Terminal 3% growth retains 21% of NPAT.

bear.growth_rationale: The credit cycle that 1H26 flagged (CIC +46% HoH, $300m forward-looking top-up, an underwritten DRP to rebuild CET1) turns in FY27-28: housing and agribusiness stress, NZ stays weak, rate cuts compress NIM to ~1.65% (FY2022 level) and broker competition takes Personal Banking share. NOI grows 1-2%.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27-28 CIC at ~12% of NOI (~33bp; FY2020 was 47bp) with CTI drifting to 47.5% on remediation and technology remediation spend: 100 - 47.5 - 12 + 0.7 = 41.2. Recovers to CIC 8.5% (~23bp) and CTI 48% (no productivity offset, ongoing outage/compliance spend): 43.5 + 0.7 = 44.2.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin 30.5% x g / ROTE 10% = 3.05 x g; FY27-28 held at 6.0% despite 1-1.5% growth because RWA migration in a downturn consumes capital the model must top up (the 2020 precedent: NAB raised $4.25bn at the trough).

scenario_narratives.base: NAB compounds net operating income at 3-4% fading to 2.5%, its business-bank franchise (one in four SMEs) growing faster than a repricing mortgage book. Cost-to-income holds ~46.5% as the >$450m productivity programme funds technology and compliance, and credit impairments normalise to ~19bp of loans. Cash earnings reach ~$7.4bn in FY27 and ~$9.4bn by FY36; 68-80% of them are distributed. At a 9.7% cost of equity and a 12.5% return on tangible equity the franchise is worth ~1.4x tangible book, not the ~2.05x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: Business and Private Banking sustains 8-9% growth with share gains, the proprietary channel passes half of mortgage flow and Personal Banking margins stabilise, BNZ recovers with the NZ economy, and AI/digital cost-out takes CTI to ~44% with credit still benign. ROTE lifts to ~14%. Even this case does not reach the current price at a 9.7% cost of equity; the market is pricing NAB's earnings as bond-like.
scenario_narratives.bear: The turn that 1H26 hinted at arrives: impairments run at ~33bp for two years across agribusiness, construction and commercial property, NIM falls to ~1.65% on rate cuts and deposit competition, payroll remediation and technology remediation keep CTI near 48%, and capital is rebuilt through further DRP underwrites (dilutive at 2x book). Growth stalls at 1-2% and ROTE settles at ~10%, barely covering the cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: 1H26 carried three early-cycle signals at once (credit impairment charge +46% HoH with a $300m forward-looking top-up, an underwritten DRP to rebuild CET1, and cash ROE 8.5% statutory), plus open operational and conduct liabilities (repeated digital outages, payroll remediation with the Fair Work Ombudsman, AML/CTF reform). Bull cut to 25%: it needs cost-out, benign credit and Personal Banking margin stabilisation to all hold for a decade, and at 2.05x tangible book the market already prices most of it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A big-four bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at an AUD cost of equity, never on statutory operating cash flow (which is deposit and loan movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. Cash earnings ex large notable items are the flow; capital retention is the reinvestment; 9.7% is the return an owner requires. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a 12.5% return on tangible equity and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~1.4x tangible book, so the 2.05x the market pays embeds either a mid-teens ROTE NAB has not earned since FY2015 or a cost of equity in the low 7s.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 10bp on the impairment charge is ~$800m pre-tax (~8% of cash earnings); the 1H26 charge annualised at ~18bp against 11bp in FY2025
Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$960bn of interest-earning assets is ~$480m of NOI (2.2%); RBA/RBNZ easing and broker competition both point down
Share count: the ~46m DRP shares are ESTIMATED from $1.8bn at ~$39; if the DRP priced lower the count is higher and value per share lower (each $1 of DRP price ~1.2m shares, ~0.04%)
Regulatory capital: the 1.5% RWA LAC step-up from Jan-2026, AT1 phase-out from Jan-2027 and any RBNZ change to BNZ's capital settings raise retention above the modelled g/ROTE
Operational and conduct: payroll remediation (>$380m to date, total uncertain), repeated outages (Sept 2026), AML/CTF and scams-framework compliance spend sit in the margin path only at run-rate
Valuation regime: Australian bank multiples have decoupled from ROE-based models since 2023 (CBA at ~3x book); the model is not a call on when that regime ends

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (ASX regular close); 52-week range 35.48-49.45.
data_sources.financials: NAB.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, AUD millions, FY2016-FY2025 annual + H1 FY2016-H1 FY2026 halves) exported from NAB.AX.duckdb; kpis table for Deposits, NetInterestIncome, NonInterestIncome, OperatingExpenses, CreditImpairmentCharge, CostToIncomeRatio, NetLoansAndAdvances, CashTaxesPaid; FY2025 Annual Report (NAB.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt) five-year summary (7875-7912, 10951), share count (17666-17700), equity-based compensation (13252), lease liabilities (17603); 1H26 report (NAB.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) cash-earnings P&L (703-725), NTA and cash ROE (780-810), CET1 and DRP underwrite (652-660, 5304), share count and diluted shares (7232-7243, 7402-7409), intangibles (4538).
data_sources.qualitative: NAB.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-24): three-priority strategy, 1H26 large notable item, credit and NIM risks, regulatory calendar (LAC, AT1 reform, RBNZ), Goldman Sachs Sell-to-Hold, September 2026 outage, bull/bear cases.
